accessibility.text: the person’s decision to be with God
Let’s turn to our last option: rejecting Proportionality.

The instructor of an introductory philosophy class has tired of the diversity of final grades for students from which he is forced to choose, and decides to simply his grading scheme. He decides that every student with a final average of 89.50 or greater will receive an A, and every student with a final average lower than that will receive an F.
the person’s faith and trust in God
the number of sins someone has committed
Despite this, as Sider points out later in the article, a parable from the Bible might be used to cast doubt on Proportionality.
the paradox of heaven and hell
the number + seriousness of sins someone has committed for which they have not repented
Isn’t it plausible that this professor is unjust precisely because he has decided to treat very similar students very differently?
the number of sins someone has committed + how serious they are
